citation.title: A complete Physics-Informed Neural Network-based framework for structural topology optimization
citation.authors: Hyogu Jeong; Chanaka Batuwatta-Gamage; Jinshuai Bai; Yi Min Xie; Charith Rathnayaka; Ying Zhou; YuanTong Gu
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 417, 116401

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The CPINNTO framework produces compliance values described as comparable to traditional SIMP designs for two- and three-dimensional cases.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 4.1 reports total CPINNTO computation time at least 312 times longer than SIMP, equivalent to classical time / CPINNTO time ≤1/312 ≈ 0.0032; this is an underperformance ratio, not a speed advantage.
claim.alternatives: Section 5 claims fewer than half as many iterations as SIMP for computationally intensive 3D problems, while Section 4.1 reports much longer total runtime; Table 1 shows compliance differences of 1.48%–11.42% against SIMP with Heaviside projection.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP, with SIMP plus Heaviside projection also compared
baseline.implementation: Open-source 88-line MATLAB code by Andreassen et al.; CPINNTO outputs evaluated with same interpolation and TO settings (Section 4.1)
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel Core i7-10700 CPU 2.90 GHz, 16 GB DDR4 RAM (Section 4)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Core i7-10700 CPU 2.90 GHz, 16 GB DDR4 RAM (Section 4)
baseline.problem_size: 2D beam 80×40 elements (Section 4.1); 3D cantilever 40×20×20 and bridge 60×20×10 hexahedral meshes (Section 4.6)
baseline.classical_time: SIMP total time reported as at least 312× shorter than CPINNTO; Table 2 gives per-case totals (Section 4.1)
baseline.ml_time: CPINNTO total time reported as at least 312× longer than SIMP and 34× longer than SIMP + Heaviside (Section 4.1)
baseline.training_time: PINNs trained per problem; included in reported total runtime; separate training duration not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not applicable: no labeled data used (abstract)
baseline.quality_metric: compliance; volume fraction; maximum von Mises stress for constrained case
baseline.quality_gap: Table 1: SIMP + Heaviside compliance is 1.48%–11.42% lower than CPINNTO in four cases; 3D CPINNTO compliance is up to 6% lower and 8% higher than SIMP (Section 4.6)

R1.evidence: Section 4.1 and Table 1 compare same load cases and target volume fractions, but CPINNTO compliance differs from SIMP + Heaviside by 1.48%–11.42%; exact matched-quality runtime is not established.

R2.evidence: Section 4.1 uses the open-source 88-line SIMP code, and Section 4 states a shared CPU; no text establishes a weak classical solver or overlong iteration count.

R3.evidence: Section 2 trains the DEM-PINN and S-PINN within each topology optimization problem; cost is part of the reported per-problem runtime, with no offline dataset training.

R4.evidence: Sections 4.1 and 4.6 evaluate returned designs with SIMP/COMSOL finite-element analyses and state volume constraints; Section 4.2 notes one nonconverged shallow network, but failure rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Four 2D beam configurations; additional 2D passive-element and stress-constrained cases; two 3D problems; network and mesh-size studies (Section 4)

notes: Open version on the University of the Sunshine Coast repository, CC BY-NC 4.0. The primary abstract comparison is quality based; the runtime comparison in Section 4.1 shows substantial underperformance.
